note:
Paper 77, Team 38720, sixty-one pages, a 2015 paper on searching for a plane lost over the ocean. Forty-seven measured regions: thirty-eight exhibit rows and nine refusals, nothing unaccounted and nothing unresolved. The paper prints thirty-seven numbered figures and every one of them is here; the thirty-eighth row is the aircraft specification grid on p16, which is pasted in as a picture and never numbered.

The one thing to know about this paper is that no caption reaches the text layer. All thirty-seven captions are painted into the pictures, so every one was read off the crop and typed in, and the layer's whole contribution to the census is a single sentence on p27 that happens to begin with the words 'Figure 11'. Three of the captions are bare - 'Figure 6', 'Figure 34', 'Figure 35', 'Figure 36' - with no title, no colon and nothing after the number.

What is drawn is a simulation study's whole apparatus. Six search methods are presented in the same three-beat rhythm - a schematic of the vector rule, one sample trial and a histogram of the search times across a hundred runs - and only the first of the six breaks it, because its paths never finish and so never produce a search time to bin. Around them sit the search-geometry figures, all drawn in one shared frame - a blue search box on a miles grid with a red centreline - and a small block of Bayesian figures on distributions instead of paths.

Two exhibits are pictures rather than charts: the p18 radar console screenshot, which is the only raster in the census and carries the barest caption in the paper, and the p8 infographic, five cells of four different kinds - a world map of missing aircraft, a bare count, two pies and a year timeline - pasted in whole from the Aviation Safety Network. The p16 aircraft specification grid is a fourth kind: a printed table preserved as an image, which is why it is a table-as-figure row and not a table row.

Three printed tables are missing from the record and that is a declared gap, not an oversight: the Lost Plane Variables grid on p13, the Search Variables grid on p14 and the Discovery Uncertainty variables on p41 are drawn as closed rule boxes of twenty-nine, thirty and fourteen rules, and the region pass returned nothing on any of those pages even though it flagged them. No measured region exists, so no table row could be anchored there.

Citation is the weakest part of the paper. Twenty-eight of the thirty-eight exhibits are never named in prose at all; the nine that are get a parenthetical pointer at best, and only Figures 25 and 26 share a sentence. The figure numbers do run in order and nobody skips, which is more than several papers in this lane manage.
rules: The single finding of this paper's census is that not one caption is quotable: the text layer holds thirty-seven numbered figures and not one of the thirty-seven caption strings. Every caption is typeset as part of the pasted picture, or set in a face the extraction drops, so all thirty-eight rows carry typed-from-crop and none could be checked against the page text [caption.verbatim].

Families spread wide because the paper is a simulation study: eleven line plots, nine histograms, seven scatters, five schematics, two 3-D surfaces, one map, one raster screenshot, one pasted table and one five-cell infographic. No categorical bar chart, no box plot, no node-link network, no heatmap and no contour plot anywhere in sixty-one pages [geometry.family].

Numbering is 'Figure N:' for thirty-three of the thirty-seven printed figures and the bare 'Figure N' with no colon and no title for four of them: Figure 6 under the radar screenshot, and Figures 34, 35 and 36 under the three confidence-interval plots [caption.numbering].

Every caption prints BELOW its picture without exception, thirty-eight rows in and not one above; the pasted aircraft grid on p16 is the only region whose label stands above it, and that label is a heading, not a caption, so it is recorded with numbering none and position above [caption.position].

Citation is almost absent: of thirty-eight rows only nine are ever named in prose (Figures 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 25, 26, 27 and 28), and eight of those nine names are inside a parenthesis in a sentence that also carries something else. Twenty-eight rows carry an empty mention. Every one of the nine is cited on the page it prints on: no figure leads or trails its citing sentence by even one page [mention.count].

Two figures share one citing sentence - Figures 25 and 26, 'A three-dimensional (Figure 25) and two-dimensional graph (Figure 26) of the initial distribution are displayed below' - which is the only sentence in the paper that names two figures at once [mention.count].

Three variable-definition grids print on pp13, p14 and p41 and NONE of them is in the measured roster: the region pass returned no region on any of those three pages although each carries twenty-nine, thirty and fourteen long rules. They are declared here as the paper's table gap rather than recorded as table rows, because no measured region exists to anchor them [place.area_frac].

The exhibits come in matched runs, and the runs are the real structure: the five later search methods each get a vector-generation schematic, a single trial and a search-time histogram, in that order and with no exception - Figures 10, 11, 12 for the bounded random, 13, 14, 15 for the weighted, 16, 17, 18 for the striped, 19, 20, 21 for the spiral and 22, 23, 24 for the sinusoidal. The first method, the completely random one, gets only the first two, because the paper says most of its simulations never finish and no mean can be established, so no histogram could be drawn [place.doc_order].

One frame carries most of the paper: sixteen of the thirty-eight rows are drawn inside the same blue-bordered search box on x 0-550 and y +-100 miles with the red centreline across it, from Figure 4 through Figure 33, so the same rectangle is redrawn sixteen times with different marks inside it [geometry.family].

Legend placement splits cleanly: eight rows carry a key box outside the frame on the right (Figures 8, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 34, 35 and 36), four carry theirs inside the picture (Figures 1, 2, 6 and 37), and the other twenty-six print no key at all [geometry.legend].

Area does not separate exhibit from furniture: the refusal on p1 measures 0.206 of the sheet, larger than the paper's first numbered figure, and five of the nine refusals are inline equation strips under 0.03 that were measured only because the picture is a raster [place.area_frac].

Section paths are assembled by hand: the heading index returns the table of contents on pp2-3 as headings, misses all eight printed 'Solution N.N.N:' headings because they are set in the body face, and returns the running word Conclusion seven times as a heading. Each path here is the printed chain with its matching page [place.section_path].
